name: Engagement Terminal Logging - tmux-logging
command: git clone https://github.com/tmux-plugins/tpm ~/.tmux/plugins/tpm   # then add tmux-logging plugin to ~/.tmux.conf
description: Capture every command and its output during an engagement with the tmux-logging plugin. Terminal logs are essential evidence: they let the client correlate your activity with their alerts, prove what was and wasn't tested, and back up your findings and timeline. Running without logging is unprofessional and can leave you unable to answer post-engagement questions.

examples.label: Reload config, then install plugins with prefix + I
examples.command: tmux source ~/.tmux.conf   # then press <prefix> I inside tmux

examples.label: Keep long scrollback so nothing is lost

variations.label: Toggle logging / dump history for the current pane
variations.command:
# <prefix> shift+p  -> start/stop logging to a file
# <prefix> alt+shift+p -> save the entire visible history

variations.label: Quick alternative without tmux
variations.command: script -a engagement-$(date +%F).log   # append all terminal I/O to a file

notes: tmux-logging writes everything typed into a pane to a log file - invaluable for the Activity Log and Payload Log sections of a report, and for recreating an attack path. Also track things you tried that did NOT work: in a low-finding engagement, that narrative shows the client what they are adequately protected against. Change the default log path and key bindings via the plugin's configuration docs. Pair with a per-command timestamp habit for defensible evidence. This is a methodology/evidence card, not an attack.

recommended.note: Where these logs live in the evidence tree.
